topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section welcomes students, introduces the lecture series, and outlines the core learning outcomes on cancer etiology.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Heredity, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental biology of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease while evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, lifestyle exposures, and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis: Initiators, Promoters, and Specific Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how diverse biological, physical, and chemical agents drive malignancy through direct DNA damage, metabolic activation, tumor promotion, and host tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Balancing Carcinogenic Risk
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding section summarizes the lecture's key concepts and frames carcinogenic exposure in terms of real-world risk-benefit decisions.
